task.prompt: Pick a name for the new internal microservice that reconciles ledger entries against the sync backlog.
task.proposed_action: name the service 'ledger-sync' after its domain

gold_label.rationale: No decision in the corpus constrains how an internal microservice is named. The only artifact is RFC 2119, which by its own abstract "defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents" — normative vocabulary ("MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", ...) for standards prose, saying nothing about service naming. The adherent behaviour is to proceed with the domain-based name without inventing a prohibition. This catches hallucinated/false prohibitions: RFC 2119 is dense with prohibition-shaped language ("MUST NOT", "SHALL NOT"), so a retriever will surface it and an arm that over-applies those keyword definitions as if they governed the task fails here with false_prohibit. On retrieval/typing, the discriminator is inverted relative to the supersession class: every arm sees the same single artifact, and adherence turns on not manufacturing a governing decision from topically prominent normative text. Gold label authored from the immutable RFC text (rfc-editor.org) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
